contract_plain_english: Equation (1.6) packages the pressure-velocity acoustics equations by taking q = (p,u)^T and the constant matrix A = [[0,K],[1/rho,0]], so that q_t + A q_x = 0 is exactly system (1.5).

binders: Real-valued unknown functions p(x,t) and u(x,t).
Constant real material parameters K and rho.
The two-component state q and constant 2 by 2 matrix A.
conclusions: With q = (p,u)^T and A = [[0,K],[1/rho,0]], the component equations (1.5) are written as q_t + A q_x = 0.
definitions_and_conventions: p is pressure, more precisely perturbation from a background constant pressure.
K is the bulk modulus of compressibility and rho is density.
The vector ordering is q_1 = p and q_2 = u; matrix rows and columns follow this ordering.
hypotheses: p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0.
rho is admissible for the reciprocal 1/rho in the physical density setting.
implicit_context: The medium is one-dimensional and the system is homogeneous, linear, and constant-coefficient.
All matrix and state entries are real.
Enough differentiability is assumed for q_t and q_x to exist.

details: Pressure is the first component and particle velocity is the second component.
K occupies the pressure-equation coupling entry A_12 and 1/rho occupies the velocity-equation coupling entry A_21; diagonal entries are zero.
Matrix multiplication of A by q_x reproduces exactly the two equations in (1.5).

undebatable_constraints: The state vector must be ordered q = (p,u)^T.
The matrix must be A = [[0,K],[1/rho,0]], with zero diagonal entries.
K must occupy the upper-right entry and 1/rho the lower-left entry.
The matrix form must be q_t + A q_x = 0 and must reproduce both equations in (1.5).
K and rho are material constants, so A is constant in this passage.
